# `nish/net/tls`

The server side of a TLS 1.3 handshake (RFC 8446), from the client's first ClientHello to its Finished, carrier-agnostic and sans-IO.

```ts
import {
  TLS_LEVEL_APPLICATION,
  TLS_LEVEL_HANDSHAKE,
  TLS_LEVEL_INITIAL,
  TLS_MAX_HANDSHAKE_MESSAGE,
  TLS_SECRET_BINDER_KEY,
  TLS_SECRET_CLIENT_APPLICATION,
  TLS_SECRET_CLIENT_FINISHED,
  TLS_SECRET_CLIENT_HANDSHAKE,
  TLS_SECRET_EARLY,
  TLS_SECRET_EXPORTER,
  TLS_SECRET_HANDSHAKE,
  TLS_SECRET_PSK,
  TLS_SECRET_RESUMPTION,
  TLS_SECRET_SERVER_APPLICATION,
  TLS_SECRET_SERVER_HANDSHAKE,
  TLS_SECRET_TO_BE_SIGNED,
  TLS_STATE_CONNECTED,
  TLS_STATE_FAILED,
  TLS_STATE_WAIT_CLIENT_HELLO,
  TLS_STATE_WAIT_FINISHED,
  TLS_STATE_WAIT_SIGNATURE,
  TLS_STATE_WAIT_TICKET,
  TlsP256Signer,
  TlsSecretPool,
  TlsServer,
  TlsServerConfig,
  tlsEcdsaDerSignature,
  tlsHeldClone,
  tlsHeldCopyIn,
  tlsHeldCopyOver,
  tlsIsZeroSecret,
  tlsSignEcdsaP256,
  tlsZeroHeld,
} from "nish/net/tls";
```

```ts
import { TlsServer, TLS_LEVEL_INITIAL } from "nish/net/tls";

const server = new TlsServer(config, serverRandom, x25519Private);
const alert: i32 = server.receive(TLS_LEVEL_INITIAL, bytes, 0, n);
// …and for the slot's next connection:
server.restart(nextRandom, nextPrivate);
// send server.takeOutput(TLS_LEVEL_INITIAL), install the handshake
// secrets, sign server.signatureInput(), call server.sign(signature), …
```

<scalar-detail title="Carrier-agnostic">

The server reads and writes handshake *messages*, not
records or packets. Bytes go in and come out tagged with the level they
belong to — Initial (cleartext: ClientHello, ServerHello), Handshake
(EncryptedExtensions through both Finished messages) or Application — and
the secrets for each level are readable as soon as they are known. TLS over
TCP (WP34 T2) wraps a level's bytes in records protected under that level's
secret; QUIC (Q2) puts them in CRYPTO frames of the matching packet number
space (RFC 9001 §4.1.3). Neither needs anything else from here.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Sans-IO">

Nothing here reads a socket, a clock or the random device. The
server random and the ephemeral x25519 private key are constructor
arguments, so a test injects RFC 8448's and a server draws them with
`crypto.getRandomValues`. Signing is handed off the same way: once the
Certificate is written the server stops at `TLS_STATE_WAIT_SIGNATURE`, the
caller signs `signatureInput()` with its own key (`tlsSignEcdsaP256` for a
P-256 key) and hands the signature to `sign`. That keeps the private key out
of this module, and it lets RFC 8448's trace, which signs with RSA-PSS, be
replayed with its own signature.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="What is negotiated">

TLS 1.3 only. The suites `TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256`,
`TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256` and `TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384`, the first of
them the client lists; the group x25519; the configuration's one signature
scheme. A client that offers x25519 in `supported_groups` without a share
gets one HelloRetryRequest (§4.1.4), and a second ClientHello still without
the share is refused. `server_name` is read and exposed as `serverName`.
ALPN picks the first of the configuration's protocols the client offers.
`quic_transport_parameters` is read and written only when the configuration
says the carrier is QUIC. 0-RTT and client authentication are not here:
an early-data offer is ignored.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Resumption">

A server the carrier calls `enableTickets` on, over TCP
only, resumes with a session ticket in `psk_dhe_ke` mode (RFC 8446 §2.2,
§4.2.11) and issues one after each handshake. The ticket keys and the
strike register are the program's, lent to each call and never kept: a
ClientHello that offers a ticket stops at `TLS_STATE_WAIT_TICKET`, and
`resume` reads the identities in the client's order, verifies the binder of
the one it selects, records its id, and answers a resumed flight — or a full
handshake when no identity can be used (`docs/security/tls.md`,
"Resumption"). Once connected, `issue` writes one NewSessionTicket at the
Application level. Sealing draws the ticket's nonce and `issue` the
`ticket_age_add` from the random device; nothing else here does. Over QUIC
the hand-off is never called, so a PSK offer gets a full handshake.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-callout type="warning">

**Refusals are alerts.** `receive` and `sign` answer 0 or a TLS alert
description (`TLS_ALERT_*` in `nish/net/tls/codec`); after one the server
is in `TLS_STATE_FAILED` and answers the same alert to every call. Nothing
the peer sends can make it panic.

</scalar-callout>

<scalar-detail title="Secrets">

Every secret the server holds is a `Secret` (`nish:secret`):
the ECDHE secret and the words it is computed in, wiped on every path; the
ephemeral key, copied into the `ephemeral` field by `restart` with the
caller's array zeroed; and the handshake, traffic, exporter and resumption
secrets, and a resumed handshake's PSK, early secret and binder key, fields
of the two `TlsSecretPool`s, read only inside `expose`.
`wipe` zeroes them all, and `restart` calls it before the next connection;
the carriers call it when a connection ends, and `wipeSecret` and
`wipeEphemeral` as each secret's work is done. `fail` wipes the resumption
master secret and the PSK's secrets, and `issue` the resumption master
secret once the ticket is sealed (CLAUDE.md §Security; TLS-1 in
`docs/security/tls.md`).

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Memory">

A `TlsServer` keeps its state in buffers it allocates once —
the messages in and out, the transcript, the secrets, the HKDF scratch —
and `restart` hands them to the next connection, so a carrier that keeps
one per slot runs every handshake after the first without moving the arena
(TLS-3; `tests/link/net_tls_memory`). What a message allocates on the way
dies inside a `using a = arena()` block or an arena scope of its own.

</scalar-detail>

The state is a class and a `switch`, with no closures. Written from RFC
8446, RFC 7301, RFC 6066 and RFC 9001, not ported from another
implementation.

## tlsEcdsaDerSignature

An ECDSA signature `r || s` (32 bytes each, as `nish/crypto/p256` answers
it) as the DER `ECDSA-Sig-Value` a CertificateVerify carries (RFC 8446
§4.2.3), or `null` when `rs` is not 64 bytes.

```ts
function tlsEcdsaDerSignature(
  rs: u8[],
): u8[] | null
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="rs" type="u8[]" required>

The signature's `r` then `s`, 32 big-endian bytes each.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="u8[] | null">

A fresh array of 8 to 72 bytes holding the DER encoding, or `null`.

</scalar-field>

A plain copy of a held secret, for a derivation that runs on its bytes

</scalar-field>

</scalar-field>

## tlsHeldCopyIn

Overwrites the bytes a `Secret` holds with `from`'s, for `exposeWith` to run on the destination.
Only as many bytes as the shorter of the two holds are copied; the rest of `held` is left as it was.

```ts
function tlsHeldCopyIn(
  held: u8[],
  from: u8[],
): i32
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="held" type="u8[]" required>

The destination's exposed bytes, written in place.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="from" type="u8[]" required>

The bytes to copy in, read from index 0.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

0.

</scalar-field>

## tlsHeldCopyOver

Copies the bytes one `Secret` holds over another's, for `exposeWith` to
run on the source with the destination as its argument: no plain copy is

## tlsIsZeroSecret

Whether an x25519 shared secret is all zeros, reading every byte (run inside `expose`).

```ts
function tlsIsZeroSecret(shared: u8[]): boolean
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="shared" type="u8[]" required>

The exposed shared secret, `X25519_SIZE` bytes.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

True when every byte is zero (a low-order peer share, RFC 7748 §6.1), which the handshake refuses.

</scalar-field>

## tlsSignEcdsaP256

Signs a CertificateVerify input for `ecdsa_secp256r1_sha256` with the P-256
private key `priv`: `p256SignSha256` (RFC 6979's deterministic nonce), DER
encoded. `null` for a malformed key. The answer is what `TlsServer.sign`
takes. The key is borrowed, as every `Secret` parameter is: the caller made
it, and wipes it.

```ts
function tlsSignEcdsaP256(
  priv: Secret<u8[]>,
  content: u8[],
): u8[] | null
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="priv" type="Secret&lt;u8[]&gt;" required>

The server's P-256 private key, borrowed.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="content" type="u8[]" required>

The CertificateVerify input, as `TlsServer.signatureInput` answers it.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="u8[] | null">

A fresh array holding the DER signature, or `null` for a malformed key.

</scalar-field>

## tlsZeroHeld

Wipes the bytes a `Secret` holds, for `exposeWith` to run on one secret of a holder outside its `wipe()`.

```ts
function tlsZeroHeld(held: u8[], answer: i32): i32
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="held" type="u8[]" required>

The exposed bytes, zeroed in place.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="answer" type="i32" required>

The value to hand back, so a caller can wipe and answer in one expression.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

`answer`, unchanged.

</scalar-field>

## TlsP256Signer

Signs CertificateVerify inputs for `ecdsa_secp256r1_sha256` with nothing
kept per signature: `tlsSignEcdsaP256`'s answer, made in a
`P256SignScratch` and handed back in one of this signer's own arrays, one
per DER length (8 to 72 bytes), since `TlsServer.sign` takes the
signature's length from its array and stores what it computes, so a
signature it is handed cannot be a temporary. A carrier keeps one signer,
not one per slot: signing is synchronous, and the array it answers is read
by `sign` before the next signature replaces it.

```ts
class TlsP256Signer
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new TlsP256Signer()` | Makes the signer's scratch and one signature array per DER length, so a signature keeps nothing: the P-256 step releases what it allocates per call, and the DER is written into one of these arrays. |
| `sign(priv: Secret<u8[]>, content: u8[]): u8[] \| null` | `tlsSignEcdsaP256(priv, content)`, byte for byte, in the array of this signer's that has its length; `null` for a malformed key. It keeps nothing: the P-256 signature releases what it allocated, and the DER is written in place. The key is borrowed. |

## TlsSecretPool

The secrets of one connection under one hash, as `TlsServer` holds them
in `secrets256` and `secrets384`: an array of exactly `hashLength` bytes
for each, allocated once and reused by every connection. The ten the key
schedule derives are `Secret`s (`nish:secret`), read only inside `expose`
and wiped by `wipe`, so the checker proves no copy of them leaves the
pool and that `wipe` reaches every one. The expected client Finished and
the CertificateVerify input are what the wire carries, and stay plain;
`wipe` zeroes them too (TLS-1).

```ts
class TlsSecretPool
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new TlsSecretPool(hashLength: i32)` | Allocates every array of the pool once, all zero, so a connection never allocates one for a secret. |
| `readonly binderKey: Secret<u8[]>` | The binder key, from the selected ticket's early secret. |
| `readonly clientApplication: Secret<u8[]>` |  |
| `clientFinished: u8[]` | The client Finished's `verify_data`, known once the server's Finished is written. |
| `readonly clientHandshake: Secret<u8[]>` |  |
| `readonly early: Secret<u8[]>` | The PSK early secret, on a resumed handshake only. |
| `readonly exporter: Secret<u8[]>` | `exporter_master_secret` (RFC 8446 §7.5), for a caller's own exporters. |
| `readonly handshake: Secret<u8[]>` |  |
| `readonly psk: Secret<u8[]>` | The PSK the selected ticket opened to, on a resumed handshake only. |
| `readonly resumption: Secret<u8[]>` | `resumption_master_secret` (RFC 8446 §7.1), derived by `sign` and the connection's once the client's Finished is accepted: what a NewSessionTicket's PSK would be derived from. |
| `readonly serverApplication: Secret<u8[]>` |  |
| `readonly serverHandshake: Secret<u8[]>` |  |
| `toBeSigned: u8[]` | The CertificateVerify input, 98 bytes longer than the rest. |

## TlsServer

One TLS 1.3 server handshake. Make one per connection, or one per slot and
`restart` it for each connection the slot takes; feed it what the client
sends with `receive`, send what `takeOutput` answers (or what the output
buffers hold, for a carrier that reads them in place), and sign when the
state says so.

The fields are readable: `state` and `alert`, the negotiated `suite`,
`serverName`, `alpn` and the client's `clientTransportParameters`, and the
`held` bits of the secrets derived so far. The secrets themselves are
`Secret` fields of `secrets()`, read through `expose`; `readKnown` and
`writeKnown` say whether the traffic secrets of a level are known yet.

**What it allocates.** Everything it keeps is allocated by the constructor
and reused by `restart`: the input and output buffers, the transcript's
hashers, the HKDF scratch, the ephemeral key's 32 bytes, and HashLen bytes for every secret
under each hash, which each derivation writes over in place and `wipe`
zeroes before the next connection starts. `receive` and
`sign` do their work inside `using a = arena()` blocks, so the compiler has
proved that what they allocate on the way dies before they return. Four
things grow or are made outside those blocks: the input buffer, doubled up
to the largest message when a ClientHello does not fit (once per slot);
the Handshake-level output, when a signature is longer than an ECDSA one;
the `serverName` string, made when the client's host name differs from the
last one this server held; and, over QUIC only, the array the client's
transport parameters are copied into, which grows only when a client's
are longer than any before (TLS-3).

```ts
class TlsServer
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new TlsServer(config: TlsServerConfig, serverRandom: u8[], ephemeralPrivate: u8[])` | A server for one connection under `config`, with the 32-byte server random and the 32-byte x25519 private key drawn for it. A random or key of another length, or a configuration `tlsConfigFits` refuses, leaves the server failed with `internal_error` before it reads anything. |
| `alert: i32` | The alert the server failed with, or 0. |
| `alpn: string` | The ALPN protocol chosen, one of the configuration's, or empty. |
| `clientTransportParameters: u8[]` | The client's `quic_transport_parameters`, opaque; empty unless the carrier is QUIC. |
| `config: TlsServerConfig` |  |
| `readonly ephemeral: Secret<u8[]>` | The connection's x25519 private key, copied in by `restart` and wiped by the record layer once the ServerHello is written. |
| `exchange: TlsExchangeWords` | The exchange's words (`tlsExchange`). |
| `held: i32` | Which of the negotiated pool's secrets the handshake has derived: bit `1 << TLS_SECRET_*` for each. A secret wiped by `wipeSecret` keeps its bit, since its place is still the one it was derived into. |
| `input: u8[]` | The bytes received at the current level and not yet a whole message: `input[0 .. inputLength)`. |
| `issuing: TlsTicketState` | What `issue` seals; its PSK is zeroed once sealed. |
| `opened: TlsTicketState` | What the ticket `resume` is reading opened to; its PSK is zeroed once read. |
| `resumed: boolean` | Whether this connection resumed a ticket (row 1 of the record's table). |
| `retried: boolean` | Whether a HelloRetryRequest was sent, so a second miss is fatal. |
| `salt: u8[]` | The salt the handshake secret is extracted under, HashLen bytes of it: the `TLS_DERIVED_SALT_*` constant on a full handshake, derived from the PSK early secret on a resumed one. `exchangeKeys` reads it into the exchange's words and zeroes it. |
| `secrets256: TlsSecretPool` | The secrets under each hash (`TlsSecretPool`); `secrets()` answers the negotiated hash's. |
| `secrets384: TlsSecretPool` |  |
| `serverName: string` | The client's `host_name`, or empty. |
| `state: i32` |  |
| `suite: i32` | The negotiated cipher suite, or 0 before the first ClientHello is read. |
| `tickets: boolean` | Whether the carrier turned resumption on with `enableTickets`; kept across `restart`. |
| `enableTickets(): void` | Turns resumption on: from the next ClientHello, a hello offering a ticket in `psk_dhe_ke` waits in `TLS_STATE_WAIT_TICKET` for `resume`, and a connection whose client lists `psk_dhe_ke` may be issued a ticket by `issue`. Kept across `restart`. A QUIC server never resumes, so on one this does nothing. |
| `issue(key: Secret<u8[]>, info: TlsTicketKeyInfo, now: i64): boolean` | Once the handshake is done, at most once a connection: seals a ticket for it under `key`, which `info` describes, and writes the NewSessionTicket carrying it at the Application level, for the carrier to send under the server's application keys. Answers whether one was written: none is when tickets are off, the client did not list `psk_dhe_ke`, or the key does not seal. On a connected connection's first call the resumption master secret is wiped before it returns, written or not, so a carrier that issues no ticket still calls this, or `wipeResumption`. Before the handshake is done, or on a second call, it answers false and touches nothing: a secret wiped then would leave no ticket to issue, and one wiped already has nothing left to wipe. |
| `known(index: i32): boolean` | Whether the handshake has derived secret `index` (`TLS_SECRET_*`) for this connection. |
| `readKnown(level: i32): boolean` | Whether the secret the server *reads* `level` under — the client's traffic secret, `clientHandshake` or `clientApplication` of `secrets()` — is known yet. The Initial level has none: it is cleartext in TLS, and QUIC derives its own from the connection id. |
| `receive(level: i32, data: u8[], off: i32, len: i32): i32` | Takes the handshake bytes `data[off .. off + len)` the client sent at `level`, a whole message, part of one or several, and handles every message they complete. Answers 0, or the alert the server fails with.<br><br>A level other than the one the state expects is `unexpected_message`, as is a byte left over once a message ends the client's flight: each of the three messages a client sends here (two ClientHellos and a Finished) is the last of its flight, and RFC 8446 §5.1 forbids a message to straddle a key change. A window outside `data` is `internal_error`, the caller's fault and not the peer's. Once the handshake is done, any further bytes are `unexpected_message` too: the post-handshake messages a client may send (KeyUpdate) belong to the record layer, which handles them itself. |
| `restart(serverRandom: u8[], ephemeralPrivate: u8[]): void` | Starts the next connection in this server's buffers, with its own 32-byte random and x25519 private key, as a fresh `TlsServer` would: every secret the last connection left is wiped (`wipe`) and none is held. The random is kept, as the constructor keeps it; the key is copied into `ephemeral` and the caller's array zeroed with `secureZero`, so the only copy left is the one the server wipes. A random or key of another length, or a configuration `tlsConfigFits` refused, leaves the server failed with `internal_error`. |
| `resume(current: Secret<u8[]>, currentInfo: TlsTicketKeyInfo, previous: Secret<u8[]>, previousInfo: TlsTicketKeyInfo, strikes: TlsTicketStrikes, now: i64): i32` | In `TLS_STATE_WAIT_TICKET`: reads the hello's tickets under the keys the carrier lends, `current` and `previous` with what each `info` says of them (a program with one key passes it as both), records the one it resumes in `strikes`, and answers the hello, resumed or in full, as the table of "Resumption" in `docs/security/tls.md` says. A selected ticket whose binder fails is `decrypt_error`, with nothing recorded (row 9). Answers 0, or the alert the server fails with. |
| `secrets(): TlsSecretPool` | The pool of the negotiated hash: SHA-384's for a SHA-384 suite, SHA-256's otherwise. |
| `sign(signature: u8[]): i32` | Takes the signature over `signatureInput()`, as it goes on the wire (DER for ECDSA), and writes CertificateVerify and the server's Finished, after which the application secrets are known. Answers 0, or `internal_error` when called in another state or with an empty or over-long signature. The signature is not checked here: a wrong one is the caller's bug, and the client's verification is what catches it. |
| `signatureInput(): u8[] \| null` | What CertificateVerify signs (RFC 8446 §4.4.3), while the state is `TLS_STATE_WAIT_SIGNATURE`; `null` at any other time. |
| `takeOutput(level: i32): u8[]` | The handshake bytes written at `level` since the last call, in a fresh array, and forgets them. Bytes are only ever written at a level whose secrets are already known, so a carrier that installs keys as they appear can always protect what this answers. A carrier that reads the output buffers in place (the record server and QUIC, inside the standard library) forgets them with `clearOutput` instead, and allocates nothing. |
| `wipe(): void` | Wipes every secret the server holds: the ephemeral key and both pools. `restart` calls it, and the carriers when a connection ends. |
| `wipeEphemeral(): void` | Zeroes the ephemeral key, which the record layer does once the ServerHello is written: not while a hello that offers a ticket waits for `resume`, whose exchange still needs it. |
| `wipeResumption(): void` | Wipes the resumption master secret, which `sign` derives ahead of the client's Finished. `issue` calls it once the ticket is sealed, and the carrier when a connection ends, closed or failed, without one (TLS-1). |
| `wipeSecret(index: i32): void` | Zeroes secret `index` of `secrets()` once a carrier has taken what it needs from it; it stays known. |
| `writeKnown(level: i32): boolean` | Whether the secret the server *writes* `level` under — `serverHandshake` or `serverApplication` — is known yet. |

interface, so a caller writes it as an object literal.

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `alpn: string[]` | The ALPN protocols the server speaks, most preferred first. Empty means the server does not negotiate ALPN over TCP, and refuses every client over QUIC, where ALPN is mandatory (RFC 9001 §8.1). |
| `certificateChain: u8[][]` | DER certificates, leaf first. At least one. |
| `extraExtensions: u8[]` | Extensions this module does not interpret, already encoded (each a type, a length and a body), written first in EncryptedExtensions: `record_size_limit` is the record layer's, for one. Empty for none. |
| `quic: boolean` | Whether the carrier is QUIC, which turns `quic_transport_parameters` on both ways. |
| `quicTransportParameters: u8[]` | The server's transport parameters, opaque, sent in EncryptedExtensions only when `quic`. |
| `signatureScheme: i32` | The signature scheme the caller's key signs with, sent in CertificateVerify: `TLS_SIGNATURE_ECDSA_SECP256R1_SHA256` for a P-256 key. A client that does not list it is refused with `handshake_failure`. |

## Limits

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="65,536" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_MAX_HANDSHAKE_MESSAGE: i32`

The longest handshake message accepted, in bytes. A ClientHello carrying a
post-quantum share is a few kilobytes; nothing a client sends a TLS 1.3
server comes near this, and the cap is what bounds the buffer a peer can
make the server hold.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>

## Constants

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_LEVEL_APPLICATION: i32`

Under the application traffic secrets: the one NewSessionTicket `issue` writes.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_LEVEL_HANDSHAKE: i32`

Under the handshake traffic secrets: EncryptedExtensions through both Finished messages.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_LEVEL_INITIAL: i32`

Cleartext: ClientHello, HelloRetryRequest and ServerHello (QUIC's Initial packets).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="11" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_SECRET_BINDER_KEY: i32`

The binder key (§4.2.11.2), held until the binder is compared.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="3" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_SECRET_CLIENT_APPLICATION: i32`

`client_application_traffic_secret_0` (RFC 8446 §7.1): the client's first application keys.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="6" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_SECRET_CLIENT_FINISHED: i32`

The client Finished's expected `verify_data` (RFC 8446 §4.4.4), plain, since the wire carries it.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_SECRET_CLIENT_HANDSHAKE: i32`

`client_handshake_traffic_secret` (RFC 8446 §7.1): the client's Handshake-level keys.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="10" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_SECRET_EARLY: i32`

The PSK early secret (RFC 8446 §7.1), held until the handshake secret's salt is derived from it.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="5" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_SECRET_EXPORTER: i32`

`exporter_master_secret` (RFC 8446 §7.5), for a caller's own exporters.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_SECRET_HANDSHAKE: i32`

Which secret of a `TlsSecretPool` an index names: what `TlsServer.known`,
`wipeSecret` and the pool's `zero` take, and the bit of `TlsServer.held`
that says the secret is derived (`1 << index`).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="9" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_SECRET_PSK: i32`

The PSK a ticket opened to, held from the binder's check to the early secret's extract.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="8" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_SECRET_RESUMPTION: i32`

`resumption_master_secret` (RFC 8446 §7.1), what a NewSessionTicket's PSK is derived from.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="4" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_SECRET_SERVER_APPLICATION: i32`

`server_application_traffic_secret_0` (RFC 8446 §7.1): the server's first application keys.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_SECRET_SERVER_HANDSHAKE: i32`

`server_handshake_traffic_secret` (RFC 8446 §7.1): the server's Handshake-level keys.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="7" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_SECRET_TO_BE_SIGNED: i32`

The CertificateVerify input sits beside them: 98 bytes and the transcript hash.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="3" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_STATE_CONNECTED: i32`

The client's Finished verified. Application data may flow both ways.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="4" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_STATE_FAILED: i32`

An alert was answered; `alert` holds it, and every later call answers it again.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_STATE_WAIT_CLIENT_HELLO: i32`

Waiting for a ClientHello at the Initial level, the first or the one after a HelloRetryRequest.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_STATE_WAIT_FINISHED: i32`

The server's flight is written; waiting for the client's Finished at the Handshake level.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_STATE_WAIT_SIGNATURE: i32`

The Certificate is written; `signatureInput()` is ready and `sign` is due.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="5" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_STATE_WAIT_TICKET: i32`

A ClientHello offered a ticket to a server with tickets on; `resume` is due, with the keys and the strike register.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>
